data.title: India-US trade deal close to completion: Goyal amid fresh tariff threat
data.description:
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Friday said the India-US trade deal is nearing completion, with the process and roadmap for finalising the pact, which had earlier held up negotiations, now taking shape.

"The US trade deal is close to culmination. The process and pathway, which was always something which held back finalising the deal, is now taking some shape," Goyal said while addressing the India Debt Capital Market Summit 2026 virtually.

The remarks came after the latest US Trade Representative's (USTR) report proposed 25 per cent tariffs on imports from India, with a provision to cap them at 17 per cent if the two countries agree to a bilateral trade deal, giving it a slight edge over Asian competitors.

data.title: Delimitation Bill: What it proposes for Lok Sabha and women's quota rollout
data.description:
The Union government has called Parliament to reconvene from November 30 to transact essential government business, amid speculation over the introduction of the proposed Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, linked to delimitation and the implementation of women's reservation.
 
In a post on X on Thursday, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the respective Houses. The Lok Sabha has been requested to meet on Monday, November 30, while the Rajya Sabha will reconvene on Wednesday, December 2. The sittings of both Houses may conclude on December 3.
 
 
The special sitting will be an extension of the Monsoon Session. Parliament was adjourned sine die on August 13 but has not yet been prorogued, which would formally end the session.
 
The government has not disclosed the specific legislative agenda for the three-day sitting. According to news agency PTI, the Union Cabinet is expected to meet on Friday and is likely to discuss the delimitation-linked women's reservation proposal. 
ALSO READ: TVS family feud: What rights do daughters have over family business assets? 

What is delimitation and what do the proposed Bills seek to change?

 
Delimitation is the process of redrawing the boundaries of Lok Sabha and State Assembly constituencies and allocating seats based on changes in population. In India, the exercise is carried out by an independent Delimitation Commission under constitutional provisions, including Articles 81, 82 and 170.
 
Its purpose is to keep the populations of constituencies broadly equal and update the allocation of seats reserved for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs).
 
The proposed Constitution Amendment Bill seeks to change provisions governing the composition of the House of the People and the allocation of seats among states and Union Territories (UTs). Its key proposals include:
 
Increase in Lok Sabha's maximum strength
 
The Constitution currently provides for a maximum of 550 Lok Sabha members, comprising up to 530 members from states and up to 20 from Union Territories. The Constitution Amendment Bill proposes raising this ceiling to 850 members, with up to 815 members from states and up to 35 from Union Territories.
 
Delimitation based on population
 
The Constitution Amendment Bill proposes reverting to the principle of allocating Lok Sabha seats to states in proportion to their population.
 
Parliament to decide which Census is used
 
The Constitution provides for delimitation after every Census, with the exercise based on population figures from that Census. The Constitution Amendment Bill authorises Parliament to pass a law determining when delimitation will be undertaken and which Census will be used.
 
A separate piece of legislation, the Delimitation Bill, 2026, provides that the latest published Census available on the date the Delimitation Commission is constituted will be used for the exercise. This implies that the 2011 Census would be used for the next delimitation exercise.
 
Setting up of a Delimitation Commission
 
Under the Delimitation Bill, 2026, the Central government may constitute a Delimitation Commission from time to time by notification to readjust and reallocate seats in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies. The Central government will also appoint the commission's chairperson.
 

How could the proposed Bill fast-track women's reservation?

 
The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023, also known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, introduced reservation of one-third of seats in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies for women.
 
However, the quota was linked to the first Census conducted after the commencement of the 2023 Act, followed by a delimitation exercise.
 
The proposed 131st Amendment Bill seeks to remove this requirement, allowing the 33 per cent reservation to take effect without waiting for a fresh Census. Instead, it links the implementation of the quota to a delimitation exercise based on the latest published Census figures, which are currently from the 2011 Census.
 
The proposed change is aimed at enabling women's reservation in time for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections, rather than delaying its implementation until after the 2027 Census.
 
The Bill proposes changes to Article 334A, which governs the reservation of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies. Under the proposed provision, the reservation would come into force "after an exercise of delimitation is undertaken for this purpose".
 
It further provides that "the seats reserved for women shall be allotted by rotation to different constituencies in a State or Union territory". The reservation would remain in force for 15 years, unless extended by Parliament.
 

What happened when the legislation was previously put to a vote?

 
The proposed legislation failed to secure the required numbers during a special sitting of Parliament on April 17.
 
Of the 528 Lok Sabha members present and voting, 298 voted in favour of the Bill, while 230 opposed it. Under Article 368 of the Constitution, a constitutional amendment requires a special majority of at least two-thirds of members present and voting.
 
This meant the Bill needed 352 votes and fell short by 54.
 
In the current 543-member Lok Sabha, the two-thirds mark would be 362 if all members were present and voting. The ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), which has 320 members, would need support from Opposition parties to secure the required numbers.
 

What is the political arithmetic behind the Bill?

 
The political arithmetic has since changed, with 26 MPs moving out of the Opposition camp.
 
Twenty rebel Trinamool Congress MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA. Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs also joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.
 
Following its alliance with the BJP, the Shiromani Akali Dal's (SAD's) lone Lok Sabha MP is also expected to vote with the government.
 
According to a report by The Hindu, the YSR Congress is reportedly set to extend support to the government on the Bill with its four Lok Sabha MPs.
 

Why could the DMK and NCP (SP) prove crucial to the numbers game?

 
The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar), with eight MPs, could play an important role in determining whether the government secures the numbers required to pass the legislation.
 
The DMK has maintained that it would consider supporting the proposed delimitation legislation if Tamil Nadu's existing share of parliamentary representation is protected, irrespective of the increase in the total number of Lok Sabha seats.
 
"If the draft Bill clearly gives us an assurance of protecting our representation in Parliament, we may consider it," a senior MP was quoted as saying by The New Indian Express.
 
The NCP (SP), meanwhile, has indicated that it will decide its position after examining the proposed legislation.
 
According to a Times of India report, party state president Shashikant Shinde said on Thursday that the party would take a call on the delimitation Bill after it was tabled in Parliament and its MPs had examined the provisions. He also played down speculation about differences within the party over the proposed legislation.
 
Separately, according to NDTV, NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule said her party would review the proposed Delimitation Bill once it was formally introduced in Parliament and could support it if its provisions served the national interest.
 

Why is the Congress opposing the proposed delimitation legislation?

 
The Congress has opposed the proposed Delimitation Bill, 2026, with party leaders arguing that it is politically motivated, unilateral and threatens India's federal structure. The party has also criticised the government for calling a special sitting at short notice without Question Hour or Zero Hour.
 
Congress leader Jairam Ramesh alleged that the gap since August had been used for "Operation Lotus" to gather the numbers needed to pass the legislation.

data.title: 2.5 mn jobs, ₹5 meals, farm loan waiver: SP releases UP polls manifesto
data.description:
The Samajwadi Party on Thursday released its manifesto for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, promising 2.5 million government jobs over five years, a monthly unemployment allowance of ₹5,000 for graduates and an annual pension of ₹40,000 for elderly women.
 
Unveiled by party chief Akhilesh Yadav in Lucknow on Constitution Day, the manifesto, titled 'Sattais Ka Sankalp: PDA Ka Pran Patra – Jan-Man Ka Manifesto 2027', places employment and welfare at the centre of the party's electoral promises. It also proposes a caste census, a legal guarantee for minimum support prices (MSP) for 23 crops and milk, an immediate farm-loan waiver and free electricity for rural households.
 
 

Akhilesh Yadav says 'bure din' are about to end

 
Taking aim at the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Yadav said the 'Acche Din' promised by the party had not arrived and that its time in power was nearing an end.
 
"We are releasing our manifesto today because 'acche din' never came, but 'bure din' are about to go away. They know that they are about to be ousted, so their language has changed," Yadav said at the launch.
 
He also accused certain powerful groups of trying to weaken the Constitution to protect their influence. "Our country will be governed by 'samvidhan' (Constitution) and not 'manvidhan' (arbitrariness)," he said.
 

2.5 mn government jobs, ₹5,000 monthly allowance for graduates

 
Employment is one of the key focus areas of the manifesto. The  Samajwadi Party has promised 2.5 million government jobs over five years and 20-30 million employment opportunities in other sectors during the same period.
 
Graduates who remain unemployed will receive a monthly allowance of ₹5,000 until they find work. The party has also promised an annual calendar of government vacancies and a transparent, time-bound recruitment process. Recruitment involving a single examination will be completed within three months, while processes involving multiple examinations will take up to six months.
 
The party has proposed skill training for 2 million young people every year, along with an Urban Employment Guarantee Act and residential hostels for male and female students in major cities. It has also promised opportunities for Agniveers who are not granted permanent commissions in the Army.
 

Education: 26,000 schools to reopen, laptops for students

 
The party has promised to reopen 26,000 primary schools that Yadav alleged were shut by the present government. It also plans to revive its free laptop-distribution scheme for students who pass Class 12.
 
A special State Education Policy will be introduced to ensure equal access to quality education, with particular attention to PDA communities and economically weaker sections. The party has proposed Wi-Fi facilities in primary and secondary schools and an allocation of 6 per cent of the state's gross state domestic product (GSDP) to education.
 
The manifesto also promises to regularise shiksha mitras, subject to legal advice, and increase their monthly honorarium by ₹5,000. The party has pledged action against examination paper leaks and greater accountability for officials and ministers.
 

Caste census, reservation and welfare measures

 
The manifesto proposes a caste census across Uttar Pradesh to identify the social and economic conditions of different communities and frame welfare policies accordingly.
 
The party has promised to allocate 20 per cent of the state Budget to the development of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (SC/ST). It has also proposed special recruitment drives to fill vacant reserved posts and a Dalit Startup Fund.
 
One of its key proposals is 50 per cent reservation for Dalits and PDA communities in government contracts worth up to ₹50 crore. A Dalit Development Council, chaired by the chief minister, is also proposed.
 
For economically weaker sections, the party has promised Samajwadi canteens serving meals at ₹5 per plate. Elderly women, including women artisans, will receive an annual pension of ₹40,000, transferred directly to their bank accounts. Labourers, women workers and artisans have also been included in the proposed annual pension scheme.
 

Farm loan waiver, legal MSP guarantee for 23 crops

 
The party has promised an immediate waiver of farm loans and a legal guarantee for MSP covering 23 crops and milk. It has also proposed compensation for farmers growing other notified crops.
 
A fund of ₹15,000 crore will be created to ensure timely payments to sugarcane farmers. The party has promised free electricity for agricultural irrigation and up to 300 units of free electricity for rural households.
 
It has also proposed an allocation of ₹1.5 trillion for rural infrastructure development.
 

Healthcare, law and order

 
The manifesto proposes a State Health Policy 2027, with a focus on affordable healthcare and medical education. Poor and PDA patients will receive free treatment at government hospitals, while families below the poverty line (BPL) will be provided health insurance cover of ₹10 lakh.
 
District hospitals will be equipped with intensive care units and ventilators, while super-speciality hospitals will be established in all 18 administrative divisions. The party has also promised to upgrade the cancer hospital in Lucknow into a leading facility in north India, with free cancer treatment.
 
On law and order, the party has promised action against caste- and religion-based violence, crimes against women, land-grabbing networks and organised crime. It has proposed a dedicated women's policing system, village-level safety arrangements and 33 per cent representation for women in new police recruitment.
 

MSMEs, traders and workers

 
The party has promised a new Industrial Policy 2027 to revive micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), along with time-bound clearances through a single-window system.
 
A Trade Security Commission and a special police force for traders have also been proposed. For workers, the party plans to introduce a Dial 1890 Mazdoor Power Line to address grievances, including those of Uttar Pradesh residents employed outside the state. A Migrant Labour Card scheme and equal pay for equal work are also part of the manifesto.
 
Elderly construction workers will receive an annual pension of ₹40,000 and health insurance cover of ₹10 lakh.
 

Infrastructure, urban development and other promises

 
The manifesto promises four-lane roads connecting all tehsil headquarters and paved roads in every village. It also proposes round-the-clock electricity across villages, towns and cities.
 
For urban areas, the party has promised round-the-clock water supply in cities with populations above 1 million, improved drainage systems to prevent flooding, better traffic management and new greenfield townships. Measures to reduce air pollution and restore the scheme for converting Nazul land into freehold property have also been proposed.
 
Other commitments include the restoration of the Old Pension Scheme for government employees, an end to outsourcing in government departments, a Public Service Delivery Act and technology-based measures to curb corruption.
 
The party has also promised to promote tourism, develop a Heritage Arc covering historically and culturally significant cities, establish three world-class stadiums and 10 sports colleges, and introduce welfare measures for journalists and lawyers.
 
The manifesto includes promises for minority welfare, including protection against hate crimes, better representation in higher education and support for artisans and weavers. For the armed forces, it proposes free education for children of martyrs and a pension scheme for their families, while reiterating its opposition to the Agniveer scheme.
 
(With agency inputs)

data.title: Nvidia, Micron, Meta and AI: India's global investing obsession decoded
data.description:
Indian investors are discovering the world beyond Dalal Street. But if their overseas portfolios are passports to global wealth, many seem to be travelling with the same itinerary: US stocks, artificial intelligence and a handful of mega-cap technology companies.
 
That is one of the striking contrasts in Vested’s How India Invests Globally 2026 report. The platform said 51% more investors transacted this year than last, while one in four new investors made an exchange-traded fund (ETF) their first global investment. Yet AI stocks accounted for 40% of assets held by investors on the platform, suggesting that global diversification is, in practice, often concentrated around a powerful investment theme. 
 
 
The report, based on aggregated and anonymised Vested platform data alongside public sources, offers a snapshot of how its customers are investing overseas. It is not a census of all Indian investors, but it provides a glimpse into the habits forming as cross-border investing becomes easier.
 
Here are the key highlights: 
  • 51% more investors transacted on Vested in 2026 than in 2025
  • One in four new investors made an ETF their first global investment.
  •  Most traded US stocks in 2026: Micron, Nvidia, SanDisk, Meta and Microsoft
  •  AI was the largest investment theme, 2026’s trading value in AI stocks was 87% higher than in all
  • of 2025
  •  Bengaluru has the most investors, but nearly three in four live outside the top 10 cities
  • Six Gulf countries account for 71% of NRI deposits
 
The AI trade has become the neighbourhood
AI is no longer just the stock investors buy to test the waters. It has become a sizeable part of their portfolios.
 
According to Vested, 31% of new investors made an AI stock their first investment in 2026, compared with 33% in 2025. More than half of investors with a portfolio held at least one AI stock, and AI companies represented 40% of assets held. Trading value in AI stocks rose 87% between January and October 2026 compared with all of 2025. 
 
The irony is that investors may be diversifying geographically while remaining exposed to a similar set of market drivers. A portfolio of several US technology stocks can still depend heavily on the same AI spending cycle, chip demand and growth expectations.
 
The report’s sector data offers a reminder of how quickly the market’s favourite can change. In 2022, energy stocks rose 66% while the S&P 500 fell almost 20%. Technology led in four of the 10 years between 2016 and 2025, while energy led in three. No sector remained the top performer for more than two consecutive years. 
"As portfolios grow and spread across more products and countries, investing through a secure and regulated ecosystem matters more, which is why we now hold three licences in GIFT City alongside our US registrations. Our belief that this decade will be when portfolios in India become multi-country and multi-currency only continues to grow stronger. Progress means more Indian families considering opportunities around the world when planning their financial future," said Viram Shah, Founder and CEO, Vested.
 
The report also looked at who invests overseas and where they live. Investors under 35 accounted for 41%, while women represented 20% share. Investors in India’s Silicon Valley - Bengaluru - held the largest overseas portfolios on average at $17,900.
 
Among non-resident Indians (NRIs), the six Gulf Cooperation Council countries accounted for 71% of deposits by value. The UAE contributed 37%, Qatar 19% and the US 7%. NRI portfolios averaged $19,500, about 2.3 times the resident Indian average of $8,600. The gap was wider for deposits, which averaged $7,100 for NRIs and $1,900 for residents.
 
Across funded accounts, seven in ten investors deposited money more than once. Of those who returned within their first year, 76% made at least one deposit larger than their first. In 2026, repeat deposits were 2.5 times the size of first deposits. Some investors used systematic investment plans (SIPs). 
 
The new investor is starting with a basket, not a stock
One of the more interesting changes is how investors begin.
 
A quarter of new Vested investors started with an ETF rather than an individual stock. The report also says 29% of investors who began with stocks later bought an ETF.
 
The habit of adding money also appears to strengthen after the first transaction. New investors made an average of three deposits in their first 12 months. A repeat deposit was around 2.5 times the size of the first, and 76% of repeat depositors made at least one deposit larger than their initial contribution during that year.
 
DIY investors want a little help — but not the steering wheel
Vested’s data suggests investors remain keen to manage their own portfolios.
 
About 62% preferred an entirely do-it-yourself (DIY) approach, choosing their own stocks and ETFs. Another 32% combined DIY investing with managed portfolios or global funds, while 6% used managed options exclusively.
 
The hybrid investor is particularly interesting. Among those who combine DIY and managed investing, 72% held a managed portfolio alongside their own stocks, while 65% held global funds alongside their self-selected investments. 
 
Bengaluru leads, but global investing is not just a metro hobby
Bengaluru accounted for 8% of investors on the platform, around 1.5 times Mumbai’s share. Vested points to the city’s concentration of engineers, product managers and senior executives working for US-listed companies, many of whom may receive restricted stock units (RSUs) as part of their compensation. 
 
The more surprising statistic is that the top 10 cities accounted for just 27% of investors. Nearly three in four investors lived elsewhere.
 
The South accounted for 37% of investors, followed by the North at 26% and the West at 23%. 
 
The largest average portfolios were not limited to the biggest financial centres either. Vested reported an average portfolio of $17,900 in Bengaluru, $17,400 in Noida, $16,600 in Gurugram and $16,300 in Mumbai. 
 
The rupee is making the case for global assets — one way or another
 
The report tracks the rupee’s movement from ₹66.33 per dollar at the end of 2015 to ₹92.97 on November 20, 2026 — a depreciation of about 40% over the period. Over 10 years, the rupee weakened at an annual rate of 3.4%; over 20 years, 3.7%; and over 50 years, 4.8%, according to the report’s calculations.
 
That currency movement can change the rupee value of an overseas investment, even when the underlying asset’s dollar price is unchanged.
 
Vested illustrates this with a ₹1 lakh investment made at the end of 2015. By November 20, 2026, the Nifty 50 price return would have taken it to ₹3.25 lakh, while the S&P 500 price return converted into rupees would have taken it to ₹4.74 lakh. The report attributes ₹1.36 lakh of the S&P 500’s rupee value to currency depreciation. The comparison excludes dividends.
 
Global investing is still a small slice of India’s mutual fund pie
Despite the growth in platform activity, overseas investing remains a small part of the broader Indian mutual fund market.
 
The report said schemes investing overseas account for less than 1% of Indian mutual fund assets. It contrasts this with the US, where around 22% of equity mutual fund and ETF assets are in funds investing mainly outside the country. 
 
This gap indicates room for overseas investing to become a larger part of Indian financial planning, particularly for households whose future expenses may be linked to foreign currencies.
 
But the next phase may be less about buying another US technology stock and more about broadening the menu.
 
Vested’s report points to European industrial and luxury companies, Japanese manufacturers and Asian semiconductor businesses as potential sources of diversification. It also highlights UCITS funds, which can provide access to different markets and investment themes through funds domiciled outside the US.

data.title: Overseas travel insurance: What it pays for and what it doesn't
data.description:
Most travellers realise the value of travel insurance only after something goes wrong, says Priya Deshmukh, head of health products, operations and services at ICICI Lombard General Insurance.

 

By then, it is too late to buy a policy.

 

Adhil Shetty, chief executive officer of BankBazaar, says many travellers consider insurance an avoidable expense after spending heavily on flights and hotels. They often underestimate the cost of medical treatment or emergency evacuation abroad.

 

Why it matters

 

One of the biggest financial risks during an overseas trip is falling ill. Medical treatment abroad can be expensive, and an Indian health insurance policy may not cover it, says Manas Kapoor, business head for travel insurance at Policybazaar.

 

 

Travel insurance covers eligible medical expenses up to a specified limit, called the sum insured. Table 1 compares premiums quoted on Policybazaar for a 34-year-old travelling to the US for a week, with a cover of $250,000.

 

Table 1: Travel insurance premiums for a week's trip to the US

InsurerPlanCover ($)Premium (₹)
Niva BupaTravel Comprehensive250,000809
Bajaj GeneralTravel Ace Lite – Gold250,0001,199
Tata AIGInternational Plus Gold250,0001,582
ICICI LombardTripSecure+250,0002,375

Source: Policybazaar. Quotes are for a 34-year-old travelling to the US for one week.

Premiums vary with age, trip duration and coverage. These figures are illustrative, not recommendations.

 

For some destinations, travel insurance is mandatory. Short-stay Schengen visa applicants generally need travel medical insurance of at least EUR 30,000.

 

What it pays for

 

Consider a traveller who falls ill in the US and spends three days in intensive care. Tata AIG's Silver plan covers up to $3,000 a day for intensive care, for a maximum of seven days.

 

If the hospital charges $4,000 a day, the policyholder must pay the $1,000 difference each day, or $3,000 over three days.

 

At a hospital covered by the insurer’s cashless network, the insurer settles eligible bills directly. Not every hospital abroad is part of that network, says Sunny Bhatia, national head of sales at Turtlemint. Travellers may therefore have to pay upfront and seek reimbursement later.

 

If a traveller cannot receive suitable treatment locally, the policy may cover medical evacuation to the nearest appropriate hospital or back to India, including by air ambulance where medically necessary. The expense is covered within the applicable policy limits.

 

Travel insurance can also compensate for baggage delays. Tata AIG’s Copper plan pays $50 if checked-in baggage is delayed by four hours. HDFC Ergo’s Explorer plan requires a 12-hour delay before reimbursing up to $250 for essentials such as clothes, toiletries and medicines.

 

These benefits are subject to waiting periods. If a flight is delayed by three hours but the policy requires a minimum four-hour delay, no payout is due. Kapoor says such conditions are a common reason claims fail.

 

What it does not pay for

 

Pre-existing medical conditions are an important exclusion. HDFC Ergo’s policy wording defines these as conditions diagnosed, treated or advised on by a doctor during the 36 months before the policy begins.

 

Consider someone diagnosed with diabetes two years earlier. Failure to disclose the condition when purchasing insurance could result in rejection of a related claim. Kapoor identifies non-disclosure and failure to meet deductible requirements among the main reasons for claim rejection.

 

Routine treatment, such as a consultation to adjust diabetes medication, is generally not covered, says Rakesh Kaul, chief distribution officer (retail sales) at Bajaj General Insurance. Sudden, life-threatening emergencies involving pre-existing conditions may receive limited coverage, depending on the policy.

 

War-related disruption is another major exclusion.

 

Mayank, 31, a Mumbai resident, was due to travel to Egypt when his flight was cancelled because of the war. The airline refunded the ticket, but his return flight from an airport operating normally remains valid and cannot be cancelled.

 

Would travel insurance cover the resulting loss? Standard policies generally exclude cancellations caused by war or airspace closures.

 

War and war-like situations are excluded. Some policies cover specified terrorism-related events under particular benefits, such as trip cancellation, so check the wording.

 

As Business Standard reported earlier, standard travel policies offer limited protection against war-related disruption.

 

Not all travel cover is the same

 

Three other products are often confused with comprehensive travel insurance.

 

Credit card insurance: Many cards include complimentary travel cover, though cardholders may be unaware of it. This often includes air accident insurance, which pays a benefit to the family if the insured dies in an aircraft accident. Some cards also cover lost baggage, flight delays or lost passports.

 

However, many do not cover overseas medical expenses, which Shetty considers the biggest financial risk. Benefits may also depend on whether the ticket was purchased using the card.

 

Some premium cards offer overseas medical cover, subject to conditions.

 

Credit card cover is therefore “rarely enough by itself”, Shetty says.

 

Insurance sold with flight bookings: Airlines and travel platforms offer basic plans through insurance partners. These plans usually have fewer benefits and lower coverage limits than a full policy.

 

Global health insurance: This is a different product. It covers planned treatment abroad, such as cancer care or a transplant, and some plans cover emergencies too. It generally costs considerably more and does not cover travel-related inconveniences such as lost baggage or flight delays.

 

Table 2: How the four types of cover differ

ProductWhat it typically coversCommon gaps
Overseas travel insuranceMedical emergencies, evacuation, baggage loss or delayWar-related cancellations, routine treatment of pre-existing conditions, delays below specified limits
Credit card insuranceAir accident benefits; sometimes baggage loss and flight delaysOverseas medical costs under many plans; benefits may require payment using the card
Flight-booking add-onBasic travel-related risks with lower limitsSeveral benefits available under comprehensive policies
Global health insurancePlanned treatment abroad, such as a transplant; some plans cover emergencies tooBaggage loss, flight delays and other travel-related losses

Coverage and exclusions vary by policy.

 

What to do to get paid

 

During a medical emergency abroad, contact the assistance provider named in the policy as soon as possible, Kaul advises. Bhatia says travellers must also inform the insurer within the period specified in the policy.

 

For baggage claims, obtain written confirmation of the delay, loss or damage from the airline before leaving the airport. Bhatia says claims can be rejected when this documentation is missing or photographs of damaged baggage are unclear.

data.title: HEG Ltd shares list at 25% premium after graphite business demerger
data.description:
HEG Ltd shares, formerly known as HEG Graphite Ltd, made their debut on the bourses on Friday following the demerger of its core graphite electrode business. The stock opened at ₹587 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), a premium of ₹118.75, or 25.36 per cent, over the pre-listing value of ₹468.25.
 
On the BSE, the stock debuted at ₹580, up ₹115.95, or 24.99 per cent, against the pre-listing price of ₹464.05.
 
At listing, the company commanded a market capitalisation of ₹11,192.70 crore, according to BSE data.
 The stock soon hit the lower circuit, falling 5 per cent to ₹551 on the BSE as investors booked profits.
 
 
As per the restructuring, which came into effect in September 2026, the original listed entity (HEG Ltd) was rechristened HEG Advanced Materials Ltd following the demerger. HEG Advanced Materials shares closed 8.4 per cent higher at ₹280.55 on Thursday.
 
HEG Advanced Materials houses the advanced materials, battery energy solutions and green power businesses. 
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex down 200 pts, Nifty around 25,800; PSU Bank, Metal up 1% each
 
The graphite electrodes business moved into the resulting company, HEG Graphite Ltd, which was later renamed HEG Ltd. It will be a pure-play graphite electrodes company.
 
Notably, the demerger of HEG Ltd was first announced in 2024, and the board later fixed September 7, 2026 as the record date. Under the demerger scheme, HEG Ltd issued shares of the resulting company to eligible shareholders in a 1:1 ratio.
 
Earlier, the company had said that the reorganisation would give each business an independent listing, focused management and the flexibility to pursue its own growth path.
 
As part of the same scheme, Bhilwara Energy Ltd was amalgamated into HEG Advanced Materials Ltd and dissolved without winding up. HEG Advanced Materials Ltd issued eight equity shares of face value ₹2 each to existing shareholders of Bhilwara Energy Ltd for every seven equity shares of face value ₹10 each held in the company.
 
According to a report by Aditya Birla Money, HEG has installed capacity of 100kt, operating at more than 90 per cent utilisation, and generating Ebitda/t of $840 – this equates to ₹7.4 billion of implied Ebitda, which compares with an Ebitda of ₹3.9 billion in FY26. 
 
It noted that the company is expanding capacity by 15kt to 115kt with a planned commissioning in FY29 and capex outlay of ₹6.5 billion. Also,  With an imminent price hike of $$1,000/t though offset partially by increase in raw materials and energy costs, the brokerage believes that HEG Ltd could deliver Ebitda/t of $1,200-1,300/t over FY28-30E.
 
These two drivers (volumes growth and price cycle recovery), could result in Ebitda potentially reaching ₹11-12.5 billion by FY28/29E, nearly doubling from the current implied run-rate of ₹7.4 billion, Aditya Birla Money said in its report.
 
 Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: WhatsApp partners with Jio, Verizon, more to bring travel eSIM data plans
data.description:
WhatsApp is introducing a feature that will allow users to buy and install data eSIMs for international travel without leaving the messaging app. The feature is intended to help travellers access mobile data abroad without having to purchase a local SIM card at an airport or rely on public Wi-Fi.
 
Announcing the feature, WhatsApp said it is working with eSIM providers and telecom operators, including Reliance Jio, Smart Axiata, Smart Communications and Verizon, among others. The company will begin rolling it out in select countries soon, although it has not specified the markets or a launch date.

How will WhatsApp's travel eSIM feature work?

The feature will allow users to discover, purchase and install a travel data eSIM directly through WhatsApp. This is expected to reduce the need to visit a carrier's store or a third-party website to arrange mobile data before travelling abroad.
 
ALSO READ: WhatsApp rolls out scheduled messages: How to use it and what to know
Once installed, the travel eSIM will provide data connectivity at the user's destination. Travellers will be able to continue using WhatsApp with their existing phone number, without having to switch their account or register a new number for the messaging service.
 
According to WABetaInfo, the feature will be accessible through the app's Account section, where users will be able to explore data plans for their destination and complete the purchase. The feature is being prepared for both Android and iOS.
 
WhatsApp has not disclosed the available data allowances, plan durations or prices. It has also not detailed how the plans will be priced across different destinations.

WhatsApp partners with Jio and other telecom providers

To support the service, WhatsApp is working with several eSIM providers and telecom operators. The partners named in its announcement include:
  • Reliance Jio
  • Smart Axiata
  • Smart Communications
  • Verizon
  • Other eSIM providers and telecom partners
The availability of plans will depend on the markets and providers supported by WhatsApp. Although Reliance Jio is among the partners, the company has not confirmed whether India will be among the first countries to receive the feature.
 
WhatsApp said the rollout will begin in select countries soon. Users will see the option within the app when the feature becomes available to them.

When will WhatsApp travel eSIM plans be available?

WhatsApp has not announced a specific launch date or a list of countries where the service will initially be offered. The company said it will begin rolling out the feature in select markets soon, with availability indicated directly within the app.
 
WABetaInfo reported that the feature is being prepared for Android and iOS devices. However, WhatsApp's official announcement does not specify supported devices or operating system requirements.
 
The move expands WhatsApp's role beyond messaging and calls by bringing mobile data plan purchases into the app. It also gives the company another way to integrate services from telecom operators and eSIM providers into its platform.

data.title: AI adoption could put 24 million knowledge-worker jobs at risk: JP Morgan
data.description:
Artificial intelligence (AI) could put around 24 million knowledge-worker jobs at risk worldwide over the next five years, as businesses increasingly use the technology to automate tasks currently performed by employees, according to a report by JP Morgan Wealth Management.
 
The estimate is based on an illustrative scenario in which companies use AI to replace a portion of their workforce rather than simply improve productivity. However, the report cautions that the impact may be felt more through reduced hiring and unfilled vacancies than through large-scale layoffs.
 

AI and employment

 
According to the report, the potential displacement represents around 1.3 per cent of the global knowledge workforce every year over five years.
 
 
This estimate assumes that half of enterprise spending on AI goes towards replacing jobs that would otherwise have been filled, while AI costs approximately half as much as the workers it replaces.
 
The impact could be particularly significant if job losses are concentrated in specific occupations or regions, as this could create wider economic and political pressures.
 
The analysis also highlighted the potential scale of disruption in the United States. If two-thirds of the displaced jobs were located there, around 16 million workers could be affected over five years, equivalent to approximately three million annually.
 
This would represent around 2 per cent of US payrolls each year, more than four times the pace of manufacturing job losses during the 2000s. ALSO READ: WhatsApp rolls out scheduled messages: How to use it and what to know 

How AI may reshape work

 
Despite the potential scale of displacement, the report said the more likely outcome would be a transformation of existing jobs rather than their complete elimination.
 
The report noted that every job involves a collection of tasks, and AI currently can automate or support only some of them. This means employees may increasingly work alongside AI tools rather than be replaced entirely.
 
It also pointed out that AI adoption across industries is likely to remain gradual and uneven, limiting the possibility of widespread job displacement in the immediate future.
 

AI adoption still low

 
The report highlighted that AI is still at an early stage of adoption, particularly outside the technology sector.
 
In the United States, around 6 per cent of work hours are currently AI-assisted, even though nearly two-thirds of tasks could theoretically be exposed to the technology.
 
For businesses to realise returns on their AI investments, adoption will need to extend beyond pilot projects and become more widespread across their operations.
 

AI use expands in India

 
The potential impact of AI on employment is also becoming increasingly relevant in India, where businesses are preparing to expand their use of the technology.
 
According to a joint report by KPMG India and the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), 93 per cent of Indian business leaders plan to deploy AI agents to expand workforce capabilities, while 59 per cent are already using them to automate workstreams or business processes.
 
The report also found that 74 per cent of Indian CEOs believe workforce readiness for AI will significantly influence business growth over the next three years. As AI takes over routine activities such as information retrieval, preparing first drafts and routine analysis, employees are expected to focus more on decision-making, interpreting information and evaluating AI-generated outputs.

data.title: APL Apollo rebounds 4% after 30% crash as Sebi may review Tata Steel deal
data.description:
Shares of APL Apollo Tubes rose as much as 4.2 per cent in early trade on Friday after the likelihood that the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) may examine the structure of its proposed deal with Tata Steel over concerns around minority shareholder interests and the applicability of related-party transaction rules. 
 
The current price rally comes after a near 30 per cent share price crash that the counter saw earlier this week following the deal announcement with Tata Steel. 
 
The company’s counter at 10:20 AM was trading 3.3 per cent higher at ₹1,531 per share on NSE. In comparison, Nifty 50 was down 0.20 per cent at 25,605.35. In intraday trade, the stock gained 4.2 per cent to touch the day's high at ₹1,544 per share.
 
 
Vipin Kumar, AVP research at Globe Capital Market, said that APL Apollo nosedived following its deal with Tata Steel. Going ahead, the sustainable support zone is placed around ₹1,280–1,260 spot levels. “Sustained trading above 1560 spot could lead to a recovery towards ₹1,650-1,660 spot levels in the short term,” he said.
 
The market regulator is weighing whether the various legs of the transaction should be assessed together under the RPT framework, including APL Apollo’s acquisition of Tata Steel’s tubes and colour-coated steel businesses, Tata Steel’s purchase of the promoters’ stake in APL Apollo, and the contract-manufacturing arrangement with promoter-linked SG Spectra. 
 
Under the transaction, APL Apollo will first acquire Tata Steel’s tubes and colour-coated businesses for ₹28,000 crore, funded through borrowings. In the second leg, Tata Steel will acquire majority control of the enlarged APL Apollo Tubes for around ₹32,267 crore by purchasing shares from the promoters and making an open offer to minority shareholders. 
 
Stakeholders Empowerment Services (SES) said Tata Steel should be considered a related party from November 23, and questioned whether the first tranche was kept below 10 per cent to avoid triggering the relevant norms.

data.title: IDFC First Bank gains 3% in subdued market; nears 52-week high
data.description:
IDFC First Bank share price movement

 
IDFC First Bank’s share price rose 3 per cent to ₹88.95 on the BSE in Friday’s intraday deals in an otherwise subdued market on expectations of healthy growth over the medium term. 
 
The stock price of the private sector lender quoted close to its 52-week high of ₹89.58 touched on September 23, 2026. In comparison, the BSE Sensex was down 0.2 per cent at 84,158.93 at 09:40 AM. A combined 7.3 million shares changed hands on the NSE and BSE.
 

Jefferies maintains ‘Buy’ rating on IDFC First Bank with TP ₹100

 
Jefferies maintains a ‘Buy’ rating on IDFC First Bank with a target price ₹100 as the brokerage firm believes that with Common Equity Tier 1 (CET-1) at 13 per cent & higher growth, the bank may consider raising capital. Expansion in return on asset (ROA) is key to rerating, the brokerage firm said, and sees 20 per cent compound annual growth rate (CAGR) in loans over FY27-29 and ROA expanding to 1.2 per cent by FY29. 
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex down 200 pts, Nifty around 25,800; PSU Bank, Metal up 1% each
 
 
IDFC First Bank’s management reiterated that the bank can continue to see 20 per cent plus loan growth in the medium-term, aided by network expansion and growth in corporate loans. Growth in deposits should be slightly higher, helping lower loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR). The bank is investing in the current account franchise through lending relationships, tech platforms & services. This can help bring down funding costs and improve corporate lending ROA, analysts at Jefferies said in a report.
 
The Bank’s net interest margins (NIMs) may be stable in near-term and can expand from Q4 aided by rate hikes. Over the medium term, NIMs may moderate as the share of lower-risk loans rises, but a positive jaws effect should open, with operating leverage aiding ROA expansion, the brokerage firm said.
 
IDFC First Bank’s robust deposit growth is expected to sustain, resulting in a higher share of lower-cost deposits in overall funding. Stronger growth in rural, retail & small and medium enterprises (SME) segments will support yields & drive margin expansion. Scale benefits will accrue over the next few years & drive a lower cost-to-income ratio as past investments start to bear fruit, e.g., credit cards. Bank has successful track record of managing retail asset quality across cycles to control credit costs, Jefferies said. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited.
